slides.title: Communication rhythm keeps the plan moving.
slides.headline: Communication rhythm keeps the plan moving.
notes: Communication rhythm is one of three execution disciplines, with priorities and keeping score.
It is how the team adjusts on real information, not stale reports. The daily and weekly meetings keep priorities, numbers and decisions moving between planning sessions.
Use the standing agendas as they are. The team can adjust the time to suit them.

artwork.alt: Generic leaders meet around a table beside a calendar of recurring meetings.

body: Run them in Metronome, using the standing agendas.

slides.title: Your meetings
slides.headline: Your meetings
notes: Daily huddle agenda: good news, then metrics. Each leader says yesterday’s widget actual and today’s forecast. Then the #1 thing to get done today, then stucks and what cannot wait. Keep problem-solving out of the huddle.
On the day of the weekly leadership meeting, the weekly replaces the huddle. Every other day the huddle runs, whoever is in.
Weekly 1:1 agenda: good news, metrics, top 3 priorities for the week, feedback both ways, then dynamic. The direct report leads it.

Weekly leadership meeting agenda: good news, values recognition, then the scoreboard review. That is last week’s widget forecast, where it landed and this week’s forecast. Then QHAG status and priority status. Finish with the dynamic part: stucks, asks and offers. Protect it. Do not cancel when busy.
Leaders carry the agreed rhythm into their own teams.

panels.heading: Daily huddle
panels.support: 7 to 10 minutes, every day except the day of the weekly meeting.
items: Metrics: yesterday’s widget actual and today’s forecast
The #1 thing to get done today
Stucks, and anything that can’t wait

panels.heading: Weekly 1:1
panels.support: 15 to 30 minutes. Each leader with each direct report, led by the direct report.

panels.heading: Weekly leadership meeting
panels.support: 60 minutes or less. The CEO owns it.
items: Scoreboard: last week’s widget forecast, actual and this week’s forecast

tip: Stucks, important information, things to mention that cannot wait.
The direct report leads it. The leader will usually have a few topics.
